channel.description: Recent content in Identity on Layer5 Documentation

item.title: Organizations
item.description:
An organization is the tenant boundary in Layer5 Cloud. It decides whose resources a request can reach, whose billing it counts against, and which roles apply. Understanding how organizations isolate, nest, and resolve explains most of what a user can and cannot see.

What an organization is 🔗

The organization is the unit of multi-tenancy and the core security boundary. Everything else composes on top of it: teams and workspaces belong to one organization, and users hold roles in it. Roles, keychains, and keys are defined once for the whole provider, but resources, billing, and access control are isolated per organization, so a role held in one organization grants nothing in another.

item.title: Teams
item.description:
A team is a named group of users inside one organization. Teams exist so an administrator can give a set of people the same access once, instead of granting it person by person. A team carries two kinds of access: roles held by its members, and workspace assignments that give the whole team access to a workspace and the resources in it.

Organizations contain any number of teams. A team has any number of members, and a user can belong to any number of teams. Teams are flat: a team cannot contain another team.

item.title: Identity and Security
item.description:
Organizations are the basic unit of multi-tenancy inside of Layer5 Cloud. The identity structure is highly flexible: organizations can have any number of teams, teams can have any number of users, and users can belong to any number of teams and organizations.

Below is an overview of the core identity components within the Layer5 Cloud.

Identity 🔗

Organizations serve as the fundamental component of multi-tenancy within the Layer5 Cloud.

item.title: Users
item.description:
User Accounts 🔗

Anyone who uses Layer5 Cloud signs into a user account. Your user account is your identity on Layer5 Cloud and has a username and profile. For example, see Five’s profile.

Five - Platform Engineer

Organization: Orbital Labs
Role: User (Platform Engineer)
Plan: Team

Curious, enthusiastic, and reliably the first to discover that a feature works differently than the docs say it does.

item.title: Account Consolidation
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud recognizes one account per verified email address, no matter which method you use to sign in.

What changed 🔗

Previously, signing in with email/password, GitHub, or Google could each create a separate account, even when they shared the same email address. This led to a confusing experience: designs, organizations, and workspaces created under one sign-in method would appear to “disappear” when you signed in with another.

item.title: Bring Your Own Mail Server
item.description:
By default, every email Layer5 Cloud sends to the members of your Organization leaves through Layer5’s shared mail server and arrives from a Layer5 address. The body of the message already carries your branding. The address it arrives from does not.

The Email tab of Edit Organization changes that. Your Organization registers its own SMTP server and its own from address, and once you have proven control of the sending domain and turned the server on, application mail such as invitations and notifications leaves through your server from your domain. Nothing about the message points to a shared provider.

item.title: Manage an Organization
item.description:
An organization is the tenant boundary in Layer5 Cloud: teams, workspaces, roles, resources, and billing all attach to one. This guide covers the administrator tasks for an organization: create it, edit its branding and sign-in settings, manage its members, move between organizations, and delete it. For what an organization is and how it relates to teams and roles, see Organizations.

Who can do what 🔗

The Organizations page opens for members who hold View Org or View All Organizations. Each task needs its own permission, and a few tasks are enforced more tightly than the permission matrix shows.

item.title: Manage Your Account
item.description:
Your profile belongs to you, not to an organization. A change applies in every organization you belong to. This guide covers the four things you can change about your account: the profile, the password, the linked sign-in providers, and the account itself.

Before you start 🔗

  • You need the View Profile permission to open the profile. The default user role holds it.
  • Changing your password needs Reset Password. Deleting the account needs Delete Account. The default user role holds both.
  • Layer5 Cloud signs you in through an identity service. Password changes and account deletion need a live browser sign-in. A script that holds only an API token cannot do either.
  • Changing a password or linking a provider is a privileged action. If your sign-in is older than the privileged-session window, Layer5 Cloud asks you to sign in again first. The window is 24 hours on hosted Layer5 Cloud and 15 minutes by default in the self-hosted chart.
  • A user’s profile can also be edited by an administrator who holds Update User Profile in an organization you share with them. Only a Provider Admin can change another user’s email address.

Edit your profile 🔗

The profile form saves itself. About one second after you stop typing, Layer5 Cloud saves the change and confirms it with a short message. There is no Save button, and edits made during a save are queued, not lost.

item.title: Your Account
item.description:
Your account is your identity across every organization you belong to. These guides cover the settings that belong to you, and the subscription that belongs to the organization you administer. For how accounts relate to organizations, sign-in methods, and roles, read the Users concept.

The account area has four tabs: Profile, Preferences, Subscription, and Plans. Each tab opens only for a user who holds its permission. Without the permission, the tab shows a permission-denied view.

item.title: Child Organizations
item.description:
A child organization is an organization created inside another organization, called its parent. A child is otherwise an ordinary organization: it has its own members, teams, workspaces, invitations, domain, and credentials. The parent relationship adds one thing, which is that administrators of the parent can manage the child’s settings and membership from the parent.

Permissions Required

Creating a child organization requires the Create Organization permission in the parent. Seeing the list of a parent’s children requires View Organizations in the parent. Editing, deleting, or adding members to a child from the parent requires the Organization Administrator or Owner role in the parent. To understand the specific roles needed for each action, please refer to the Roles and Permissions reference.

How Organizations Nest 🔗

  • An organization can have any number of child organizations.
  • A child can have child organizations of its own, and those can have children of their own. There is no limit on depth.
  • Every top-level organization sits directly under the provider organization of your Layer5 Cloud deployment. The provider organization is never itself a child, and it does not appear in the child organizations section.
  • A child belongs to exactly one parent. A child cannot be moved to another parent after it is created.

A parent administers its direct children only. An administrator of a grandparent does not administer a grandchild by virtue of that role; the administrator of the intermediate organization does.

item.title: Organization Configuration Scenarios
item.description:
Every organization in Layer5 Cloud is configured by two choices: where your users sign in (the front door) and whose identity provider authenticates them. The combinations form five named scenarios. This guide helps you pick one and then walks through the settings that implement it, including who is allowed to change each setting.

For the mechanics behind the choices, see White-labeling (themes, logos, custom domains) and Identity Services (bring-your-own-credentials and authentication boundaries).

item.title: Set Notification Preferences
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud sends email when something happens that involves you: you earn a badge, your role changes, someone comments on your design. Notification preferences decide which of those emails reach you. Preferences belong to your account, so they apply in every organization you belong to.

Email is the only channel. Layer5 Cloud has no per-event choice between email and another channel.

Before you start 🔗

You need the View Profile permission, which the default user role holds. The preferences are on your own account, and you cannot set them for anyone else.

item.title: Organizations
item.description:
These guides cover the administrator tasks for an organization, the tenant boundary in Layer5 Cloud. Each guide states which role it needs. For what an organization is and how it relates to teams, users, and roles, read the Organizations concept.

I want to Go to Role needed
Create, edit, brand, switch between, or delete an organization Manage an Organization Organization Admin or Owner; Provider Admin for domains
Nest an organization inside another and delegate its administration Child Organizations Create Organization in the parent
Send organization email through my own SMTP server Bring Your Own Mail Server Organization Admin or Owner
Choose and set up a custom domain and identity provider Organization Configuration Scenarios Provider Admin for the domain, Organization Admin for providers
Create and award organization badges Recognize Members with Badges Manage Recognitions

For the people side of an organization, see Teams, Users, and Roles.

item.title: Manage Subscriptions and Billing
item.description:
A subscription connects an organization to a Layer5 plan and bills for it. This guide covers what you can see and do with subscriptions, who can do it, and how the amount you pay follows your membership. For what each plan includes, read Feature Availability by Plan. Current prices are on the pricing page.

Who can manage a subscription 🔗

A subscription belongs to an organization, not to a person. Layer5 Cloud checks the caller against the subscription’s own organization, so administering one organization gives you no access to another organization’s billing.

item.title: Recognize Members with Badges
item.description:
A recognition is a badge that an organization defines and awards to its members. Recognitions mark milestones such as completing training, contributing to a project, or reaching a team goal. An awarded badge appears on the recipient’s public profile, where the recipient can share it.

Two kinds of badges exist, and they come from different places:

  • Organization recognitions are created and awarded by an organization’s administrators. This guide covers them.
  • Layer5 community badges belong to the Layer5 community recognition program. Browse them in the Badge Gallery and read how they are earned in the Recognition section of the Layer5 Community Handbook.

Who can do what 🔗

Task What it needs
Create, edit, or delete a recognition The Manage Recognitions permission in the organization that owns the recognition. Organization Admin, Provider Admin, and Academy Admin hold it by default. The Manage Recognitions control on the Organizations page is enabled for holders of Edit Organization.
Award a recognition to a member The permission to update that member’s profile, held in an organization you share with the member.
View a badge Anyone who can open the recipient’s public profile.

Two limits apply to every award:
